why: The server is a FIFO queue where, each second, the front request is served and any request whose deadline wait[i] equals the current time drops out. Simulating with a front pointer plus buckets of requests by expiry time gives each request one removal, so the queue size per second comes out in linear time.
hints: Write out the timeline for example 1: at each second, which requests leave the queue, and why?
At time t, the request served at t-1 leaves, and every unserved request with wait[i] == t expires. Group requests by their wait value so you can find who expires at t without scanning the queue.

Keep removed flags, a front index that skips removed requests, and buckets[t]. Each second: remove last served, remove bucket t, record the count, advance front to the next alive request. O(n + max wait).
pitfalls: The output starts with n at time 0 and ends with the 0 for the instant the queue becomes empty.
A request served at time t is still counted at t; it leaves at t+1.
A request with wait[i] = t expires at time t even if it would have been next; an already-served request must not be removed twice.
